EA.name: Expert Adherence (Training)
EA.characteristics: Player matches or cleanly outperforms the expert through the section.  - Standard adherence: the driver line stays close to the expert racing line for the whole range, speed gap stays small or returns toward parity, and the time gap has no new meaningful loss pattern.  - A time gap below 200ms is not a mistake by itself. If the time-gap facts show no meaningful rise, no worsening ending slope, no spike, and no technical-error evidence, treat the section as clean context rather than MSP or RM.  - Expert-or-better clean section: EA can still apply when the player is ahead of the expert, gaining on the expert, or using a cleaner/faster line than the expert reference, even if the line is wider or tighter. Require no off-track, cutting, instability, adverse opponent outcome, or pit-procedure evidence.  - Distinguish gap value from gap rate: a positive but flat or constant carried time gap only means the player is already behind, not that a new mistake happened inside this range.  - When the time-gap facts are unavailable, do not rule out EA solely for that reason. Use trajectory, speed, brake, throttle, segment shape, and the absence of MSP, RM, MSR, or PS evidence. Mutually exclusive with MSP and RM.

MSP.name: Mistake (Practice)
MSP.characteristics: Technical driving error causing time loss or instability, NOT caused by interaction with a close opponent.  - MSP / RM boundary is decided by whether a new mistake action or newly worsening loss rate happens inside this split section, not by the section's start index or by the time gap starting near zero. At lap or session start, a near-zero time gap is baseline context only.  - If the section contains the new mistake action (run wide, cut tight, braking or throttle error, instability, or newly worsening time-loss rate), label the section MSP even if the driver later recovers, merges back, or the whole-section ending slope is lower than the starting slope.  - Time-gap evidence must show a new or worsening loss event inside the range: the time gap ends higher, the ending slope is higher than the starting slope, the local curve has a raising run, or a spike appears in the middle. Use the start value, end value, local curve changes, reversal events, and ending-slope comparison together rather than any single endpoint.  - A rising time gap supports MSP only when it aligns with a new in-section driving error or strengthening loss rate and the absolute gap or gap change is at least 200ms. Do not infer MSP from a sub-200ms gap, an absolute endpoint value, a near-zero start, or a total endpoint change alone.  - If the range enters already compromised but the facts show a lower ending slope, shrinking end value, movement toward recovery, or only a constant carried gap while trajectory, brake, or throttle evidence shows merge-back behavior, treat that as RM or empty context rather than new MSP.  - Speed gap supports MSP when local runs or the overall value show the player falling farther from the expert, especially when those ranges align with the new mistake action and the time gap also worsens. Do not decide MSP from one isolated speed sample.  - The driver line exceeds the expert envelope because of a new in-section movement away from the expert line, either outward wide or inward tight. Recovery back toward the expert racing line later in the same section does not cancel MSP when the section began with the mistake action, but a range that begins after the mistake and primarily merges back is RM.  - In opponent-capable data, an adverse opponent outcome (failed attack or broken defense) makes the section MSR instead of MSP. Mutually exclusive with EA, RM, and MSR. The detailed-annotation flow refines MSP sub-ranges later; attach MSP at the section level when the section starts with or is dominated by a technical error that occurs inside the section.

MSR.name: Mistake (Racing)
MSR.characteristics: Time or position loss caused by an interaction with a close opponent inside the section.  - Require an opponent interaction outcome of failed attack or broken defense with medium or high confidence. Low or weak confidence means use opponent trajectory evidence cautiously or submit an empty label list.  - The primary opponent slot, nearest-opponent distance, and relative trajectory are supporting evidence for the interaction and technique.  - The time gap may grow across the interaction window, but the adverse opponent outcome is the gate. Mutually exclusive with EA, RM, and MSP. No close opponent, no primary opponent, or an outcome other than failed attack or broken defense means not MSR.

RM.name: Recovery & Merge
RM.characteristics: Player recovering from a prior mistake inside this section.  - RM / MSP boundary is decided by whether the current split section contains the new mistake action. Use RM when the section does not contain the new mistake action and the first qualifying behavior is recovery or merge from an already-carried off-line state, off-track state, instability, prior incident, or already-rising time gap.  - A preceding mistake, off-track moment, or incident explains why recovery is needed. A time gap that enters the range already rising means time loss may have begun before this section; do not treat that incoming rise as a new in-section MSP by itself. A near-zero starting value is also not MSP evidence by itself, especially at lap or session start.  - Time-gap recovery evidence comes from the start value, end value, local curve changes, reversal events, and ending-slope comparison. The time gap should end lower, or it may end higher only when the ending slope is lower than the starting slope and there is no spike or raising run in the middle.  - RM can still start with a rising time gap when the action evidence is recovery or merge and the end-of-range facts show shrinking, movement toward recovery, a dip rather than a spike, or a decreasing loss rate. Do not classify RM from speed alone if the time gap keeps worsening through the end.  - Speed gap supports RM when it stops widening, narrows, or moves toward parity during the merge-back phase, matching the time-gap recovery facts.  - The driver line trends back toward the expert racing line from a non-zero or already-compromised state, with brake and throttle action consistent with rejoining or merging back. Do NOT use RM just because an MSP section has a later recovery phase; if the section starts with a mistake action that occurs in this section, the whole parent segment is MSP and recovery is described in the reasoning or detailed child sub-segment. Do NOT attach when the player started clean with no carried mistake or off-line state; that is EA or an empty parent, not RM. Mutually exclusive with EA and MSP.

PS.name: Pit Stop
PS.characteristics: Player is in the circuit's Pit section. Pit procedure is PS even when the car is accelerating out and returning toward the racing surface.  - Require pit evidence from the selected circuit-section match, splitter context, or a top section match that overlaps the circuit's known Pit section.  - When the section evidence is ambiguous between Pit and the adjacent straight because they share a normalized range, sustained pit-lane-style trajectory offset plus large player/expert speed separation or slow pit-exit acceleration is sufficient Pit-section procedure evidence.  - Do not label PS from speed rise, low speed, trajectory offset, or acceleration back toward track speed alone when the range is in a normal racing section away from Pit. Compatible with the circuit label. Do NOT combine with EA, MSP, MSR, O, or OD.

O.name: Successful Overtake
O.characteristics: Player gained a position on a specific opponent inside the section. Multi-car positional data is the gate.  - Require an opponent interaction outcome of pass completed with medium or high confidence; the signed longitudinal relationship should show the opponent ahead at entry and behind by exit. Empty, unavailable, low-confidence, or non-pass outcomes mean do NOT attach O.  - The primary opponent slot, nearest-opponent distance, and relative trajectory support the pass evidence and identify the target car.  - Player-trace evidence can explain technique: late-brake signature past the expert reference, sustained outside or inside line deviation not explained by MSP or RM, or speed greater than expert on equal-or-less throttle. A close opponent plus failed attack is MSR at the section level; a successful defense is OD, not O.

OD.name: Successful Defense
OD.characteristics: Player held position against a real, close opponent inside the section.  - Require an opponent interaction outcome of held defense with medium or high confidence; the relative-position evidence should show the opponent threatening from behind or alongside but not getting ahead by exit. A merely close car with no held-defense outcome is not OD. Low or weak confidence means inspect opponent trajectory evidence or submit an empty label list.  - The primary opponent slot, nearest-opponent distance, and relative trajectory support the defense evidence and identify the target car.  - Player-trace evidence can explain technique: earlier braking than expert, tighter trajectory than expert for inside cover, or a throttle lift on a straight with no brake onset for defensive lift. Time gap may grow briefly during the defense as long as position holds. A defense that failed because the opponent got past is MSR at the section level.

prompt_rules.required_behavior_parent_label_rule: Every saved lap segment must include at least one behavior parent label from {{eligible_behavior_labels}}.If no required behavior parent label fits the whole split-section range, submit an empty label_ids array to drop the range instead of saving a parentless segment.

mode_exclusion_rules.practice: Pick at most one technical/recovery behavior parent from {MSP, RM}; MSP + RM is a contradiction. PS should not be combined with MSP.
mode_exclusion_rules.racing: Pick at most one opponent-aware behavior parent from {O, OD, MSR}; O + OD, O + MSR, and OD + MSR are contradictions. PS is allowed only for Pit-section procedure and should not be combined with O / OD / MSR.

interaction_focus.body: This split range {{origin}}. For this work unit, identify the target car from the splitter evidence first, then do ONLY overtake offence / defense annotation: pick O for a successful attacking pass, OD for a held defense, or MSR for a failed attack / broken defense. If the opponent evidence is only close-following/draft context, or the opponent stays tucked directly behind without a lateral/alongside threat, submit `label_ids: []` rather than labeling normal practice-driving telemetry such as EA / MSP / RM. PS is still valid when the range has Pit-section procedure evidence.

prompt_rules.task_intro: Annotate ONE lap range. The deterministic splitter handed you a fixed split-section boundary; if this is an opponent interaction window, the boundary is event-shaped and circuit sections are context only. Your job is to include the circuit id and one selected circuit_section id from splitter or preflight context, at least one required behavior parent label for any saved segment, and an optional matching sub-label.
prompt_rules.splitter_section_context: Splitter context: `{{circuit_id}}` ({{circuit_name}}), `{{section_id}}` ({{section_name}}). Use this as the selected circuit_section unless Pit-section evidence makes the Pit section the better knowledge-base fit. If `locate_circuit_section` is ambiguous, use `top_matches` only as competing evidence to resolve to one circuit_section id.
prompt_rules.preselected_section_context: Splitter section context: `{{preselected_section_id}}` ({{preselected_section_name}}) from the opponent sub-segment; include it in `label_ids`.
selection_notes: Preflight semantic label candidates cover current-session main-label and sub-label choices.
When any main-label or sub-label signature fits only part of the range, omit that label or submit an empty `label_ids` array to drop the range.

payload_shape.intro: `payload_json` must be a JSON object of this shape:
payload_shape.reasoning_placeholder: <4-6 sentence human-readable evidence note citing ilocs, values, trends, tool verdicts, range-fit rationale, and any ambiguous option rejected>
followup: `label_ids` carries the circuit id, one selected circuit_section id, and your main / sub-label picks together. Every saved segment must contain at least one of {{eligible_behavior_labels}}; otherwise submit an empty `label_ids` array as the valid 'drop this section' signal. The runner reports back the split section range.

hard_rules: Do not invent label IDs; circuit / circuit_section ids must come from splitter or preflight context, every other id from preflight semantic candidates.

When `locate_circuit_section` reports ambiguity, choose exactly one circuit_section id using splitter context and behavior evidence. For Pit-vs-straight ties, choose Pit when Pit-section evidence supports pit procedure; otherwise choose the normal racing-surface section. A Pit-vs-adjacent-straight ambiguity plus sustained pit-lane-style trajectory offset and large player/expert speed separation or slow pit-exit acceleration counts as Pit-section procedure evidence. Do not include multiple same-range circuit_section ids.
prompt_rules.whole_range_label_rule: Every behavior and sub-label must describe the final annotation range as a whole. Do not attach a label because it matches only one phase, one apex moment, or a short slice inside the range; omit that label or leave it for detailed child sub-segment annotation.
prompt_rules.segment_action_model_rule: Evaluate the saved lap parent segment as a complete action group over the final iloc range. Driver/expert turning / trajectory, brake, and throttle comparison is required for segment completeness at entry or exit; do not treat complete action-group evidence as optional sub-label evidence.
prompt_rules.reasoning_note_rule: Write `reasoning` as a longer human annotation note: 4-6 concise sentences covering the final iloc range, selected label fit, key telemetry values or trends, deterministic tool verdicts, and why competing labels were omitted. When two plausible labels or circuit sections are ambiguous, name the option that was not selected and state why it was rejected. For time-delta prose, say `losing time run` and avoid ranking/adjective phrasing.
